verdicts.summary: The new modelCatalogOnly branch is safe. The empty providers list never reaches client state, older servers are never sent the flag, and the call stays a separate single-flight entry from full refreshes.
verdicts.scenario: I tried three cases. (1) A web picker opens and the server answers { providers: [] }; does the client wipe its provider or workspace-snapshot state? onSuccess returns early because neither caller passes instanceId or cwd, and the config stream is untouched. (2) A new client talks to an old server that would ignore the field and run a full refresh. Both clients check the modelCatalogRefresh capability first and return when it is missing. (3) A picker open lands while a full refresh is pending. The single-flight key includes modelCatalogOnly, so the open does not join the full refresh's result. On a failed fetch, lastAttemptMs is set before the fetch (ModelManifest.ts:244), so the next attempt waits out the 5-minute retry window. recoverRefreshFailure catches defects, so the RPC still succeeds and nothing is shown.

verdicts.summary: The probedManifestUpdatedAt check holds. Full passes never overlap, so an older pass cannot overwrite a newer recorded updatedAt. A real probe reads the current manifest, so the recorded value is never newer than what providers used.
verdicts.scenario: I tried four cases. (1) Pass A starts having read manifest X. The picker then fetches Y, joins A, and A records X. The loop sees X ≠ Y and starts pass B, which reads Y and records Y. Could a late A record X after B? No: refreshAllInFlightRef lets only one pass run at a time, and A finishes before B is claimed. (2) A concurrent forceRefresh fetches a newer Z between the fetch and the pass. The pass records Z, and the loop runs at most one redundant pass. (3) Does a pass actually pick up the new models? Yes: managed refresh calls checkProvider with forceRefresh:true (managedProvider.ts:153, 217-219), and the Codex check reads modelCatalog.current, which is the live manifest (CodexDriver.ts:234-239, ModelManifest.ts:290-293). (4) The startup value is initialManifest. The startup probe is forked using that same manifest (managedProvider.ts:365), so recording it as already probed is accurate.
